record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: For the minimality problem for positive realizations, can one obtain tight lower bounds and tight upper bounds for the minimal order, meaning the smallest state dimension of a positive realization of a given transfer function?

evidence.quote: The positive realization problem consists of providing answers to the questions: - (The minimality problem) What is a minimal value for N?
- find "tight" lower and upper bounds to minimal order of a positive realization1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H(z)$ be a rational transfer function with nonnegative impulse response, i.e., the formal power series expansion $H(z)=\sum_{k\ge 0} h_k z^{-k}$ satisfies $h_k\ge 0$ for all $k\ge 0$. A positive realization of $H$ is a triple $(A,b,c)$ with $A\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{N\times N}$, $b\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{N}$, $c\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{1\times N}$ (all entries nonnegative), such that $H(z)=c(zI-A)^{-1}b$. The minimal positive realization order of $H$ is
$$N^*(H)=\min\{N\in\mathbb{N}: \text{there exists a positive realization }(A,b,c)\text{ of }H\text{ of dimension }N\}.$$
Note that $N^*(H)$ may strictly exceed the McMillan degree of $H$.

Problem: Find tight lower bounds and tight upper bounds for $N^*(H)$ as a function of computable invariants of $H$ (e.g., the poles, residues, and McMillan degree of $H$); that is, exhibit explicit functions $L(H)\le N^*(H)\le U(H)$ that can be achieved with equality on families of transfer functions, and ideally a procedure to compute $N^*(H)$ exactly.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and papers (including a 2022 survey in Automatica and 2025 work on positive Markov realizations) confirm that determining the minimal order of a positive realization remains open in general; only various lower and upper bounds are known, with no tight characterization for arbitrary transfer functions. Tight necessary and sufficient conditions have been obtained only in special cases (e.g., third-order systems with real poles).

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive realizations: A survey
status_evidence.snippet: Only lower and upper bounds for the dimension of a minimal positive realization have been given to date.
status_evidence.claim: The minimal positive realization dimension is not known in general; only bounds are available.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive Markov realizations
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known, to date, how to determine in general the minimum dimension of a positive realization.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2025, the problem of finding the exact minimal order of a positive realization remains open.

status_evidence.title: An upper bound on the dimension of minimal positive realizations for discrete time systems
status_evidence.snippet: Upper bound on the dimension of minimal positive realizations.
status_evidence.claim: Research continues to provide improved upper bounds, indicating tight bounds are not yet established.
